pr.title: mir-opt: execute MatchBranchSimplification after GVN
pr.author: dianqk

processing.reason: PR #140115 is an optimization-ordering change, not a semantic miscompilation. It moves MatchBranchSimplification after GVN/SimplifyLocals::AfterGVN so structurally identical branch arms can be merged. The added match1 test demonstrates a missed optimization now being performed; it does not demonstrate an incorrect rewrite. Every other MIR diff is pass-specific local renumbering or StorageLive/StorageDead placement (e.g. _5/_6 role swaps, _7/_8/_9 additions, canonicalized transmute copies), not a value-semantics change. Any original/transformed function pair that produces differing results would have to fabricate a transformation the PR never performed, which is disallowed.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `run_optimization_passes` scheduled `&match_branches::MatchBranchSimplification` after SROA and before `MultipleReturnTerminators`, `GVN`, and `SimplifyLocals::AfterGVN`. The patch removes `&match_branches::MatchBranchSimplification,` from that earlier position and adds it after `&simplify::SimplifyLocals::AfterGVN,`. Thus MatchBranchSimplification previously ran before GVN had canonicalized equivalent computations, so `if c { v1 - v2 } else { v1 - v2 }` was not collapsed and the conditional remained in MIR.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: This is an optimization PR, not a demonstrated incorrect rewrite. The historical behavior was a missed transformation: MatchBranchSimplification was placed too early, so branch bodies that become structurally identical after GVN were left as separate branch targets instead of a single direct computation. The PR fixes this by running MatchBranchSimplification after `&gvn::GVN` and `&simplify::SimplifyLocals::AfterGVN`. The description says it fixes only the first example; it does not claim `match2` with `v1 - 1` is fixed.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR functions used in mir-opt tests where a boolean condition selects between arms performing the same pure computation. Supplied positive example: `pub fn match1(c: bool, v1: i32, v2: i32) -> i32 { if c { v1 - v2 } else { v1 - v2 } }`. Supplied non-fixed comparison: `if c { v1 - 1 } else { v1 - 1 }`. Existing test domains include transmute/indexing in `issue_75439.foo` and local/StorageLive/StorageDead handling in `simplify_locals_fixedpoint.foo`.
analysis.summary: Relocating MatchBranchSimplification after GVN and SimplifyLocals::AfterGVN exposes canonicalized identical branch bodies; `match1` with identical `v1 - v2` arms becomes a direct `_0 = Sub(...)` in pre-codegen MIR. Test changes also reflect local numbering and pass-specific expectation churn, not a new incorrect rewrite.
analysis.trigger: Run MatchBranchSimplification after GVN and after SimplifyLocals::AfterGVN, so equivalent successor blocks have been canonicalized before MatchBranchSimplification compares or merges them. In the added test, both arms compute `v1 - v2`, and the pre-codegen result is `_0 = Sub(copy _2, copy _3);` followed by `return;`.
preconditions: Pipeline order places `&match_branches::MatchBranchSimplification` after `&gvn::GVN` and `&simplify::SimplifyLocals::AfterGVN`, rather than before `MultipleReturnTerminators` as in the removed ordering.
Both branch successors must be equivalent after canonicalization; the positive test uses a bool condition with identical `v1 - v2` arms.
MIR assertions should target the relevant pass output or PreCodegen output, e.g. `// EMIT_MIR matchbr.match1.PreCodegen.after.mir`.
Do not assume all source-identical-looking arms are optimized: the PR description lists `match2` but says the PR fixes the first case only.
pitfalls: Do not infer a wrong MatchBranchSimplification rewrite from this PR; the source frames it as providing more optimization opportunities, and the historical issue is pass ordering.

Do not treat local renumbering and StorageLive/StorageDead changes in the Inline and InstSimplify expectations as semantic changes; for example `_5` and `_6` swap roles in `unchecked_shifts` and `unwrap_unchecked` diffs.

Pass-specific dumps can change appearance after reordering: the SimplifyLocals diff adds `let mut _7: bool;` and removes `StorageLive(_6);` / `StorageDead(_6);` even though the final optimization goal is MatchBranchSimplification after that pass.

The existing `issue_75439.foo.MatchBranchSimplification.diff` expectation changes to canonicalized copies such as `_2 = copy _1 as [u32; 4] (Transmute);`; do not use the old temporary-move form as the intended output.
Do not overgeneralize from the `match1` test to constant-arm forms like `v1 - 1`, which the description explicitly leaves as a separate, unfixed case.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a rustc mir-opt pre-codegen test using `// EMIT_MIR matchbr.match1.PreCodegen.after.mir`, with `// CHECK-LABEL: fn match1(`, `// CHECK: bb0:`, `// CHECK-NEXT: _0 = Sub`, and `// CHECK-NEXT: return;`. Use two programs differing only in the branch bodies: identical `v1 - v2` arms as the positive case, and a control such as the supplied `v1 - 1` arms or non-identical arms to avoid overclaiming. Update expected MIR diffs for MatchBranchSimplification after GVN and for SimplifyLocals local/StorageLive expectations. Exercise both panic-abort and panic-unwind where MIR diffs are maintained. No compiler was built or executed here.
evidence: This can provide more opportunities for MatchBranchSimplification.
Currently, rustc does not optimize the following code into a single statement at mir-opt, and this PR fixes the first case.
if c { v1 - v2 } else { v1 - v2 }
